title: Pure dimension of a Cartier divisor on an integral finite-type scheme
statement:
Let k be a field, X an integral finite-type k-scheme of pure dimension d>=1
[def-weil-pure-dimension], and J an invertible ideal sheaf defining an effective
Cartier divisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. Then every irreducible
component of J.subscheme has dimension d-1, i.e. J.subscheme has pure dimension
d-1. The empty divisor is included, with its vacuous purity condition.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2: hypersurface purity, isolating one irreducible component

proof.text: Finite type over a field makes X Noetherian. Its irreducibility and purity give total dimension d. The closed divisor has Noetherian underlying space.

For a component Z of the divisor, remove the other finitely many components to obtain a nonempty open o of the divisor contained in Z. Since the divisor is closed embedded, o is the inverse image of an ambient open A.

The open A is integral of dimension d and finite type over k. Pullback of the Cartier ideal gives a nonempty Cartier divisor E on A. Its underlying space is o and Cartier dimension drop gives dim E=d-1.

Take a generic point z of Z. The reduced subscheme C on closure{z} is integral: its closed embedding has irreducible image and a reduced vanishing-ideal quotient. The preimage W of o is a nonempty open of C. The closed embedding identifies W with o and C with Z topologically. Nonempty-open dimension invariance on C therefore identifies dim Z=dim W=dim o=dim E=d-1.

lean.statement:
theorem Scheme.IdealSheafData.isPureDimension_of_isInvertible
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (d : ℕ) (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hX : X.IsPureDimension d)
    (J : X.IdealSheafData) (hJ : J.IsInvertible) :
    J.subscheme.IsPureDimension (d - 1)
